------
Order No.11 Dated- 19.05.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Deoghar Town P.S. Case No. 432 of 2022 instituted under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per FIR, allegation is that petitioner is only an introducer of the land in question which has been purchased by the informant.

It is further alleged that in the name of showing the land of one Saroj Singh bearing Plot No.537, Jamabandi No.41 measuring 870 sq. ft situated near Deoghar Railway station, petitioner obtained Rs.27,66,500/- from the informant on different dates for execution of sale deed in his favour to be executed by the real vendor
but after lapse of 5 years, petitioner neither executed the sale deed nor returned the money.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that petitioner has already paid all the outstanding dues to the informant vide agreement dated 30.06.2021 (Annexure-2).

It is further submitted that one agreement to sell some land was entered into between the informant's wife and petitioner on 18.03.2022 and the informant and his wife took Rs.13 lakhs as advance money and inspite of executing the sale deed, the informant lodged this false case against the petitioner.

Petitioner has no criminal antecedents and undertakes to co-operate Kundan Thakur @ Kundan Kumar Thakur vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123955679/
1 with the investigation of the case.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submits that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner that several cheques of different dates have been issued in favour of the informant by the petitioner but the same were dishonoured due to insufficient balance in petitioner's bank account.
It is further submitted that the alleged agreement about return of money to the informant(Annexure-2) relied upon by the petitioner is a forged document.
The real fact is that the informant is going to institute a complaint against the petitioner for the offence under Section 138 of N.I. Act.
Hence, petitioner may not be extended privilege of anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record and in view of the return of consideration money to the informant and documents in question relied by petitioner shall be considered at the time of trial,
hence, I am inclined to extend privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned CJM, Deoghar in connection with Deoghar Town P.S. Case No. 432 of 2022 with the condition that he will co-operate with the investigation of the case and appear before the investigating officer as and when noticed by him and furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Pappu/
